The test image shows a cut stem section submerged in water with visible bacterial streaming (white cloudy ooze flowing down from the stem). The stem has brown vascular discoloration. This is the classic "streaming test" used to diagnose bacterial wilt diseases. Top candidates: **Bacterial_Wilt**, **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**, **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**.

Now viewing one reference per top candidate:

This is an near-identical match to the test image — same streaming test setup, same bacterial ooze, same vascular browning, sequential Bugwood image numbers (5606063 vs 5606065). Now checking Southern_Bacterial_Wilt to differentiate:
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt shows a graduated cylinder outdoors — different container and setting from the test image's beaker in dark lab. Now checking Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato:
Bacterial_Canker shows field leaf symptoms, completely different. I need one more view from a 4th class to satisfy the budget requirement:

Verticillium_Wilt shows wilted/yellowed field leaves — unrelated to the streaming test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: Cut stem in a glass beaker (dark lab background), with clear bacterial streaming (white ooze threads) and brown vascular discoloration — the classic diagnostic streaming test for *Ralstonia solanacearum*
- Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood 5606063): Nearly identical — same beaker, same dark lab, same streaming pattern, sequential image number to test image (5606065)
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt: Also shows streaming but in a graduated cylinder outdoors — different setup
- Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato: Field leaf symptoms, no streaming test
- Verticillium_Wilt: Field wilting symptoms, no streaming test

The match to Bacterial_Wilt is unambiguous — same photographic series, same diagnostic setup.
